detailed_summary: The paper addresses the practical realization of quantum estimation bounds, building on the foundational work of Monras and Paris. It proposes a scheme that leverages generalized heterodyne detection, a concept introduced nearly half a century ago, to meet the stringent real-time processing and quantum advantage requirements of next-generation quantum information technologies. The authors argue that while quantum estimation theory has been mathematically well-established, its applied progress was limited until recent decades, and their work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical bounds and practical implementation. The paper demonstrates that their proposed scheme, based on Monras and Paris's results, can effectively satisfy the demands of near-future information technologies, emphasizing strict real-time processing without delays and guarantees of quantum advantage unattainable by classical theory.
